key_insight: The paper shows that an AI agent can act like a real X-ray scientist, autonomously aligning single crystals at a synchrotron beamline. This demonstrates that large language models can drive adaptive, closed-loop experiments in high-end scientific facilities.
problem_solved: Traditional synchrotron experiments often require expert human operators to align samples and make rapid decisions during data collection. This work addresses the challenge of automating that complex, real-time experimental workflow.
method: Built an agentic AI system that uses a large language model to plan and execute experimental actions.
Connected the AI to a real synchrotron beamline so it could observe feedback and adapt decisions in a closed loop.
Demonstrated autonomous single-crystal alignment as a test case for scientific experimentation automation.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this is a strong example of LLMs moving beyond text generation into real-world scientific control systems. It highlights the potential for agentic AI to reduce manual labor, speed up experiments, and enable autonomous discovery in lab environments.

paper_title: An agentic artificially intelligent X-ray scientist
paper_authors: Zhantao Chen, Alexander N. Petsch, Aidan J. Israelski, Rajan Plumley, Lingjia Shen
